description.narrative: The project is implemented in Bosnia-Herzegovina. The main outcome areas it contributes to are democracy and human rights and gender equality. The main right holders are tenants (women, youth and underrepresented groups). Through research, information, legal aid and advocacy, the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between Center to Support Organisations (CENSOR) and the Swedish Union of Tenants (Hyresgstfreningen) Aros-Gvle. The purpose of both organisation is to improve the situation for tenants in their respective countries.Project ObjectiveThe main objectives of project interventions are to: - Improve and harmonise legal framework and legislation in housing i.e. tenancy sector in Bosnia and Herzegovina and North Macedonia by building new alliances and pushing progressive politics with the aim to create a housing market with two parts landlords and tenants - Raise awareness of tenants on their rights, responsibilities, duties and social position through advocacy activities, mitigating social tensions. - Increase climate activism among tenants, particularly students and underrepresented groups. - Empower youth to develop the living conditions and go on with the work from HOLICOB project in cooperation with youth groups in Western Balkan. Transfer of know-how i.e. existing HOLICOB methodology from B&amp,H to North Macedonia in order to improve the living conditions of youth.Actor groupsDecision makers: Parliament bodies, government and agencies at all levels. Gender centres/commissions/agencies Actors in cooperation: CSOs, media, political parties, academia Right holders: tenants, citizens, women, youth and underrepresented groups
